column1: # SLOOP JR — the 30 missions. THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for both the firmware table and the printed cards.
# tools/gen_kid_missions.py reads this file and writes build/gen/kid_missions.h and build/kid_cards.md.
# One row per mission, tab separated. Edit this, then re-run the generator (./build.sh does it).
#   done    what the header says when it completes, <= 24 characters (ui.msg, finding 28)
#   id      0..29 in order of play (the numbers here start at 1 on the cards: id + "MISSION")
#   level   1..10 (the gate level the mission belongs to)
#   title   the FONT_L heading, <= 14 characters
#   line1   the first FONT_S line, <= 28 characters ("-" = none)
#   line2   the second FONT_S line, <= 28 characters ("-" = none)
#   hint    what SEQ says (the second hint), <= 28 characters
#   bpm     the seed's tempo
#   kit     the seed's drum kit index (0 ACOUSTIC, 1 DEEP, 2 TIGHT, 3 BRIGHT, 4 DUST, 5 808,
#           6.. user kits, then SYN1..SYN4; 5 = the default)
#   parts   which tracks sound: D drums, B bass, K keys, L lead (the rest are muted)
#   drums   the seeded drum lanes: lane=steps, 1-based, '.' or '-' for none (<= 4 lanes)
#   bass    the seeded bass notes: note=step, MIDI note numbers (36 = C2) (<= 8 notes)
#   check   KEYS / LANE / WROTE / NOTEPC / BARS / PARAM / PARAMS / PRESET / LAYER / SAVED /
#           UNDONE / ENGINE / SAMPLE / HONOUR
#   arg     what the check wants: LANE lane=steps (1-based), WROTE track=count (0 bass,
#           1 keys, 2 lead, 3 drums), NOTEPC track=pitchclasses, PARAM id (or id=count),
#           PARAMS count, PRESET count,
#           LAYER LY_*, ENGINE ENGI_*, KEYS count, BARS count
#   check2  a second check that must also pass ("-" = none) and its arg
#           (the done line is informational praise, never a score: plan §5)
# The card text is printed only: it never enters the firmware.

column17: card
The white keys are a drum kit, in order: kick, kick 2, snare, clap, hat, open hat, pedal, rim. Hit them all - nothing here can break.
Kick on 1 and 3 is the heartbeat of nearly every dance record ever made. Count 1-2-3-4 and hit on 1 and 3.
ACOUSTIC, DEEP, TIGHT, BRIGHT, DUST, 808: same beat, different drum kit. Which one sounds like the music you like?
The snare on 2 and 4 is the clap you hear in every pop song. Now it is a real beat.
Hats fill the space between the beats. A quiet one (hold OCT-) makes it breathe.
Straight is 0. Push it up and the off-beats lean late: that is swing, and it is the difference between a drum machine and a drummer.
This is your instrument. Track 2 is a bass: one note at a time, low, and it holds the band up.
In a lot of songs the bass does not play melodies - it walks between three notes. C, F, G: try it under your drums.
On a double bass a slide is a real thing your hand does. Here it is one knob.
One white key now plays a whole triad - the same chord shape your left hand makes, spelled out by the machine.
Add the 7th and a plain chord becomes the sound of jazz, neo-soul and lo-fi beats.
This knob is the single most useful thing on the machine. Everything you have ever heard in electronic music does this.
Fast attack = plucked. Slow attack = a pad that fades in. Same note, different instrument.
Turn this up and the filter starts to whistle at one note. That is how acid basslines work.
An echo on one drum only: that is how dub and techno get that huge space out of a tiny room.
Reverb is the room. Small room = tight. Big room = cathedral.
Hold FX and hit a key: the music gets destroyed for a second. Let go and it is back. This is what DJs do with their hands.
Hold one note and the machine plays it over and over in a pattern. Chords become melodies.
Lock the keys to a scale and every note you press is in tune with the rest. You cannot play a wrong note.
Everything is playing - now the top line. Four notes is a melody. That is all a hook is.
This engine does not play a recording. It computes a string being plucked, right now, sample by sample. Pizzicato, basically.
Hold the key and it bows. Same maths as your bass, different hand.
Strike one note and other strings ring along without being touched. That is a sitar, and it is also why the piano pedal sounds the way it does.
Saving is the difference between playing and composing. This one is kept.
A verse and a chorus, or an A and a B. Two ideas that answer each other: that is a song.
Order is a choice. A-B-A is the oldest shape in music and it still works.
This is how a DX7 made every bell, electric piano and bass sound of the 1980s. Six little oscillators, borrowing each other's wobble.
Whatever you put in, you can play at any pitch. Record your voice, then play it as a bassline.
This one has no test. You decide when it is finished, and you play it to someone.
Ten levels. Drummer, bass, chords, melody, and a song. Now the whole machine, with nothing locked and nothing to learn next - the same one that gets updated by itself.
